ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Formulation-specific interaction

A 45-year-old man taking disulfiram is prescribed Zoloft oral concentrate because he has difficulty swallowing tablets. The pharmacist contacts the prescriber before dispensing it. What feature of this formulation creates the contraindication?

  1. Its alcohol content
  2. Its unusually high potassium content
  3. Its irreversible inhibition of aldehyde dehydrogenase
  4. Its complete absence of sertraline
  5. Its conversion of disulfiram to dopamine
Answer and explanation

Its alcohol content

The alcohol-containing concentrate is incompatible with disulfiram; formulation matters even when the active drug is unchanged.

Option explanations

Its alcohol content: The alcohol-containing concentrate is incompatible with disulfiram; formulation matters even when the active drug is unchanged.

Its unusually high potassium content: Potassium is not the interaction responsible for this contraindication.

Its irreversible inhibition of aldehyde dehydrogenase: Disulfiram inhibits that enzyme; the formulation supplies the interacting alcohol.

Its complete absence of sertraline: The concentrate contains sertraline as its active medication.

Its conversion of disulfiram to dopamine: This is not a relevant metabolic pathway.
